findings.title: Unguarded access to first destination calendar crashes when no destination calendar is set
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so it is `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar. The next line then accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. Previously this used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. Any booking with a Google Meet location and no destination calendar will throw a TypeError and fail event creation instead of falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar for every host
findings.body: `createEvent` now runs once per host/credential through `EventManager`, but this method still selects `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId`. It ignores the credential whose calendar is being created. With a collective event that has multiple hosts using Office365, every Office365 host will get an event created in the first host's selected calendar rather than in their own. The same first-element-only pattern exists in Lark and BaseCalendarService, so those integrations are also broken for multi-host collective events.

findings.title: updateLocation creates calendar references without externalCalendarId or credentialId
findings.body: `referencesToCreate` now reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` does not return either field. For calendar updates (`updateAllCalendarEvents`), the resulting reference is stored with `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId` undefined. Later cancellations/reschedules cannot target the correct calendar credential and may fall back to deleting through every calendar credential or fail.

findings.title: Only the first old calendar reference is deleted when rescheduling multi-host events
findings.body: When `newBookingId` is provided, the cleanup path still does `booking.references.find(...)` instead of `filter(...)`. A collective booking now has multiple `_calendar` references, one for each host. On reschedule, only the first old calendar event is deleted; the other hosts keep the old event on their calendars.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation only deletes the first calendar reference for each occurrence
findings.body: Inside the recurring/all-remaining branch, `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` selects only one calendar reference per updated booking. For a multi-host collective recurring booking, each occurrence has multiple calendar references. Cancelling the series will remove only the first host's event from each future occurrence and leave the other hosts' events in their calendars.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback no longer resolves the destination calendar when externalCalendarId is absent
findings.body: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it looks for an externalId of null/undefined and returns undefined. Previously the fallback used the single `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Legacy booking references without `externalCalendarId` will therefore update with an undefined calendarId (or delete from primary rather than the selected calendar). The same issue appears in `deleteEvent` below.

findings.title: Team destination calendars are silently discarded when evt.destinationCalendar is null
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op for `null`. In a collective event where the organizer has no destination calendar but the hosts do, none of the host destination calendars are attached to the event, so no calendar events are created for those hosts.

findings.title: Google organizer email uses the first destination calendar for every credential
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is always the first item in `destinationCalendar`, while `selectedCalendar` is correctly found by `credentialId`. When creating the event for the second/third host credential, the organizer attendee email is still set to the first host's `externalId`. This makes the Google Calendar event organizer incorrect for every host except the first, which can affect ownership, notifications, and invitation behavior.

findings.title: Organization slug/requestedSlug conditions are inverted
findings.body: The previous code set `slug` on the organization when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` was false, and stored `requestedSlug` in metadata when billing was enabled. This change swaps that behavior: billing-enabled environments now set `slug` directly and no longer store `requestedSlug`, while non-billing environments create the organization without a slug. This is an unrelated behavior change that can break organization creation/subdomain handling depending on the deployment configuration.
